name: bipartite_matching
author: e2346c64
description: Finds a maximum matching in a bipartite graph with the Hopcroft-Karp algorithm: the largest set of edges with no shared node, i.e. the most one-to-one pairs. Use for assignment questions: What is the best assignment of students to projects? How many students can get a project of their choice? Who is left unassigned? Works on undirected, bipartite graphs (e.g. 'projects'); sides come from the 'side' node attribute, or are found by 2-colouring. Weights are ignored. Returns an error for directed or non-bipartite graphs. Returns matching_size, max_possible, whether it is perfect, the matched pairs (up to top_k) and the unmatched nodes on each side.

graph_id.description: Id of an undirected bipartite graph, e.g. 'projects'.

top_k.description: Maximum number of matched pairs (and of unmatched nodes per side) to list.
